texts.facts: 2 Brief facts stated in the appeals bearing no. 16/13 and 17/13 are that the appellant Sh. Anil Garg is the proprietor of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers who was running the proprietorship shop, shop no. 1, 6695, East Rohtash Nagar, Shahdara, Delhi 32 and was selling the Biscuit of M/s Apsara Biscuit Company, C36/2, Lawrence Road, Delhi35. The Ashok Kumar was the Food Business Operatorcumsalesman in the proprietorship shop M/s Aggarwal Petha Store. On 22.12.2011 at about 4.30 PM Food Safety Officer Sh.P.M.Kothekar purchased a sample of "Biscuit" from the proprietor shop M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers, shop no.1,6695, East Rohtash Nagar, Shahdara, Delhi32 which was kept for sale for human consumption. The Food Business Operator cumsalesman Ashok Kumar s/o Ram Kishore was present at the shop, who disclosed that sample commodity i.e. biscuit was supplied to him by M/s Apsara Biscuit Company. The sample of the biscuit 4 x 360 grams were taken into custody and four samples of Criminal Appeal no. 16/2013 and 17/2013 3 of page 13 the same were sealed in the presence of the witnesses. Sample taken in the M/S Apsara Biscuit Company vs Dr. P.M.Kothekar on 30 September, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124598043/ 2 custody was in original sealed condition packets which was divided in four parts and all the four parts were sealed separately in presences of witnesses and accordingly, Panchnama was prepared at the spot, which was signed by Food Business Operatorcumsalesman Ashok Kumar and by the other witness Sh. Ram Pratap Singh FSO. One of the sample in intact condition was sent to Food Analyst, Delhi on 23.12.2011 and the other two sample parts were deposited with Sh. S.K.Nanda in intact condition in sealed packet on 23.12.2011. The fourth sample was also deposited with Sh. S.K.Nanda, Designated Officer as Ashok Kumar Food Business Operatorcum salesman did not request for sending the said sample to NABL Accredited Laboratory. 3 On analyzing the sample by the Food Analyst, the same was found to be misbranded. The report of the Food Analyst is PFA/Enf/1198/2011 dated 30.12.2011. The complainant sent the copy of the Food Analyst report to the Food Business Operator and M/s Apsara Biscuit Company on 12.01.2012 for their comments on the report. Criminal Appeal no. 16/2013 and 17/2013 4 of page 13 4. Sh. Ashok Kumar s/o Sh. Ramkishore (Food Business Operatorcum salesman); (2) Anil Garg s/o Sh. Deendayal Garg Proprietor of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers; (3) Sh Harish Chandra Sharma s/o Sh. Om Prakash Sharma Nominee of M/s Apsara Biscuit Company and (4) M/s Apsara Biscuit Company did not prefer for sending one counter part of the sample to the Referral Laboratory. 5. Sh. Ashok Kumar (Food Business Operatorcumsalesman) has filed affidavit in support of him stating therein that he has left the job of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers. Sh. Anil Garg s/o Sh. Deendayal Garg Proprietor of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers also filed affidavit in his support that he has not paid Sales tax and Income tax and is running a small petha shop at 1/1159, East Rohtash Nagar, Delhi 32, Sh. Harish Chander Nominee of accused no.4 M/s Apsara Biscuit Company has filed Income Tax return for the year 201011 and 201213 and thereafter, the Ld. ADM, District NorthEast, Delhi has passed the impugned order. 6 Aggrieved from the impugned order the manufacturer M/s Apsara Biscuit Company and the vendor Sh. Anil Garg proprietor of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Criminal Appeal no. 16/2013 and 17/2013 5 of page 13 Bakers preferred present appeals. 7. The grounds for appeals are that the impugned order passed by the court below is bad in law and the court below has misread the evidence on record. There is no misleading or deceptive statement or claims have been found on the label of food article and the gravity of offence as alleged is only technical in nature and does not lead to any misstatement or deception to the consumer. The fine of Rs.45,000/ on the manufacturer i.e. M/s Apsara Biscuit Company is too harsh. As per the complaint of the complainant, Dr. P.M.Kothekar, Food Safety Officer, after issuance of the notice to Sh. Ashok Kumar Food Business Criminal Appeal no. 16/2013 and 17/2013 6 of page 13 Operatorcumsalesman, has taken a sample of the biscuit on 22.12.2011 at 4.30 p.m. from the shop of M/s Aggarwal Petha Store & Bakers in presence of the Sh. Ashok Kumar Food Business Operatorcumsalesman. Sh. Anil Garg is the proprietor of the said shop. The sample was taken from one manufacturer's sealed packet in original condition which was divided in four parts and the same were sealed at the spot and got the signatures of Food Business Operatorcum salesman i.e. Ashok Kumar and Panchnama was prepared and one sample was sent to Food Analyst, Delhi on 23.12.2011. Two samples were deposited with Sh. S.K.Nanda, Designated Officer. No request received from the Food Business Operatorcumsalesman for sending the same for analysis from NABL, therefore, the fourth sample was also deposited with Sh. S.K.Nanda, Designated Officer. After analysing the sample, the Food Analyst found the sample sent to him was misbranded. The report of the Food Analyst is reproduced as under : Analysis Report i Sample Description: Apsara butter zeera biscuit sample in original sealed packet. ii Physical appearance: Brown colour sample. Iii Label: Without declaration of type of flavouring agent and size of Label (70.84 Criminal Appeal no. 16/2013 and 17/2013 7 of p cms) is only 23.69 % of the size of packet (299 sq. cms), which shall not be less that 40 %. Prescribed Standards as per:(a) Food Safety & Standards ( Food Products and Food Additive) S.N Quality Name of Method of Test Result Regulations 2011 o Characteristic used (b) As per label declaration for proprietary foods ( c ) As per provisions of the Act and Regulation, for both above 1 Test for Coaltar Dye Double Wool Dyeing Negativ () e 2 Colour identified () 4 Ash insoluble in Dil Manual Method 0.07 % Not more than 0.1 % HCL() 5 Acidity of extract fat DGHS Manual Method 0.13 % Not more than 1.5 % as Oleic Acid() Opinion : The sample is misbranded because there is violation of Regulation No. 2.2.2.5(ii)(b) and 2.3.2(b)1(a) of the Food Safety & Standard (Packaging & Labelling) Regulation, 2011.
